articles.title: Tsunami azul: o tamanho da vitória democrata nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Opositores de Donald Trump tomaram controle da Câmara e do Senado em vitória com ampla margem. Democratas conquistaram espaço em redutos republicanos.
articles.summary: Opositores de Donald Trump tomaram controle da Câmara e do Senado em vitória com ampla margem. Democratas conquistaram espaço em redutos republicanos.
articles.body:
A vitória dos democratas nas eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos , na terça-feira (3), já é marcada por números históricos. O partido ampliou a presença no Congresso, conquistou governos estaduais e avançou até em redutos tradicionalmente republicanos.

Os resultados redesenham o mapa político americano, com conquistas que não eram vistas há décadas. Também representam uma derrota importante para o presidente Donald Trump, que terá que lidar com uma oposição fortalecida nos próximos dois anos de mandato.

Da mudança no voto popular a recordes eleitorais em diferentes regiões do país, veja os números que ajudam a dimensionar o resultado das urnas.

Até a publicação desta reportagem, o placar da apuração estava da seguinte forma:

A vitória dos democratas nos Estados Unidos — Foto: Gui Sousa/Arte g1

Um dos sinais mais expressivos da mudança de cenário político está no voto popular para a Câmara. Com 89% dos votos apurados, os democratas somavam 59,6 milhões de votos, o equivalente a 54,98% do total. Os republicanos tinham 47,2 milhões, ou 43,56%.

O resultado representa uma virada em relação à eleição presidencial de 2024. Naquele ano, Trump recebeu 77,3 milhões de votos, ou 49,8% do total, enquanto Kamala Harris teve 75 milhões, equivalentes a 48,3%.

Na disputa presidencial, portanto, os republicanos terminaram 1,5 ponto percentual à frente. Agora, nas eleições para a Câmara, os democratas abriram uma vantagem de aproximadamente 11,4 pontos percentuais.

A comparação precisa levar em conta que as eleições de meio de mandato costumam ter participação menor do que as presidenciais. Ainda assim, o comparecimento também foi expressivo.

Mais de 62 milhões de americanos votaram antecipadamente, antes do dia 3 de novembro, segundo dados da Universidade da Flórida. O levantamento também indicava uma vantagem democrata entre os votos depositados antes do dia da eleição.

O candidato democrata ao Senado pelo Texas, nos Estados Unidos, James Talarico, durante campanha na cidade de Dallas, em 29 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Mike Segar/ Reuters

As pesquisas já apontavam um cenário favorável aos democratas, mas a dimensão das vitórias foi além do esperado. O partido avançou em diferentes regiões do país e conquistou espaços em estados tradicionalmente republicanos.

No Texas, os democratas conquistaram duas vitórias históricas: elegeram o primeiro senador e a primeira governadora democrata pelo estado em mais de 30 anos.

No Kansas, outro reduto republicano, o partido elegeu um senador democrata pela primeira vez em 94 anos. Em 2024, Trump havia vencido o estado por mais de 16 pontos percentuais.

O avanço também aparece em um levantamento da Reuters. A agência analisou cerca de 2.200 condados com apuração avançada e constatou que os republicanos perderam participação nos votos em 99% deles, na comparação com o desempenho de Trump na eleição presidencial de 2024.

A derrota republicana também é histórica pela dimensão da mudança no Congresso. Pela primeira vez em 20 anos, um presidente republicano perdeu o controle das duas Casas em uma eleição de meio de mandato. A última vez havia sido em 2006, durante o governo de George W. Bush.

A perda de espaço no Legislativo representa um obstáculo para Trump nos dois últimos anos de mandato.

Com os democratas fortalecidos, o presidente terá de negociar com uma oposição que ganhou poder para influenciar a agenda do Congresso e fiscalizar o governo.

A insatisfação com os republicanos também apareceu nas disputas estaduais. Pela primeira vez em 16 anos, os democratas vão governar a maioria dos estados americanos.

O partido também conquistou nove dos dez estados mais populosos do país. A Flórida foi a única exceção: será governada por um republicano. Mesmo no estado, porém, a vitória republicana ficou abaixo do que as pesquisas projetavam.

Democratas de Nova York comemoram vitória nas midterms de 2026 — Foto: Jeenah Moon/Reuters

Uma pesquisa de boca de urna da Associated Press, realizada com cerca de 80 mil eleitores nos 50 estados, ajuda a explicar parte do resultado.

O levantamento apontou que os eleitores com menos de 30 anos tinham menos probabilidade de votar em candidatos republicanos à Câmara. Entre os jovens, também era maior a parcela dos que disseram ter votado para o Congresso como forma de demonstrar oposição ao presidente.

O mesmo movimento apareceu entre os eleitores hispânicos, que demonstraram menor apoio aos candidatos republicanos em comparação com o desempenho de Trump em 2024.

A pesquisa também mostrou que economia e democracia estavam entre as principais preocupações dos americanos.

O custo de vida e a corrupção no governo tiveram peso importante na decisão dos eleitores.

Além disso, muitos defenderam que o Congresso exerça um papel mais firme de fiscalização do presidente.

Apesar de os democratas terem uma pequena vantagem em temas como economia e corrupção, a pesquisa indicou que o partido ainda não é muito mais popular do que o republicano entre os americanos.

articles.title: Cores dos partidos dos EUA: por que democratas são azuis? | G1
articles.standfirst: Tradição de associar cada partido a uma cor da bandeira americana é recente, e só entrou no imaginário do país nas eleições de 2000.
articles.summary: As cores dos partidos dos EUA nem sempre foram fixas e a tradição atual só se consolidou no imaginário popular após a histórica e apertada eleição do ano 2000.
articles.body:
As eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos , as chamadas midterms, mostrou um avanço democrata no Congresso americano. O partido fez maioria nas duas casas legislativas , além de conquistar a maioria dos governadores.

Na democracia americana, os dois maiores partidos – Democrata e Republicano – são representados, cada um por uma cor: azul e vermelho, respectivamente. A vitória maciça dos democratas tem sido chamada de "onda azul".

Eleitores votam durante as eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA, em uma seção eleitoral em Hillsboro, Virgínia, EUA — Foto: REUTERS/Tierney L. Cross

Mas nem sempre foi assim. Inclusive, a história começou com as cores invertidas: os primeiro mapas eleitorais coloridos a aparecer na TV americana mostravam em azul os estados onde os republicanos Nixon, Ford e Reagan haviam conquistado mais votos — e em vermelho os locais onde Jimmy Carter, Dukakis e até Clinton haviam conquistado maioria.

A tradição de associar cada partido a uma cor é recente na história dos EUA, e só “pegou” seis eleições atrás, no ano 2000.

Ela tem sua origem algumas décadas antes, nos anos 1970, por causa das coberturas de eleições das TVs locais.

Em 1972, quando a TV em cores começava a ganhar espaço nas casas americanas, a rede CBS começou a exibir mapas de estados coloridos em azul ou vermelho, dependendo de qual partido havia tido mais votos – e, por consequência, levaria os respectivos delegados para o Colégio Eleitoral. A emissora atribuiu a cor azul a Richard Nixon, dos Republicanos, e o vermelho para McGovern, dos Democratas.

Nas eleições seguintes, em 1976, a concorrente NBC inaugurou um grande mapa analógico para acompanhar a apuração dos votos. Ele era dotado de luzes azuis ou vermelhas para cada estado, que se acendiam conforme o partido que ganhava no local. O mapa aparecia constantemente na tela, e foi considerado revolucionário na época. A ideia foi copiada pelos concorrentes nos anos seguintes.

Novamente, os Democratas ficaram com a cor vermelha, e os Republicanos, com a azul. Em uma reportagem da revista “Smithsonian”, os produtores da NBC da época disseram que não se lembraram de discutir muito a respeito sobre qual cor ficaria com qual partido. Segundo um dos funcionários, a escolha foi feita com base no Reino Unido, que também possui um sistema mais ou menos bipartidário e cuja bandeira tem as mesmas cores da americana – onde os Trabalhistas, mais de esquerda, usam a cor vermelha, e os Conservadores, a azul.

Nos EUA, a ligação dos Republicanos com o azul data do século 19: na Guerra Civil Americana (1861-1865), essa era a cor do uniforme dos unionistas, liderados pelo então presidente Abraham Lincoln.

Mapa eleitoral da NBC News nas eleições de 1988 mostra estados republicanos em azul e estados democratas em vermelhos — Foto: NBC News/Reprodução/Mídias sociais

Ao longo dos anos 1980 e início dos 1990, cada canal de TV escolhia a forma de diferenciar os dois partidos em seus mapas eleitorais , e uma mesma emissora eventualmente trocava as cores depois de quatro anos.

Em 1980, a ABC adotou o vermelho para os Republicanos, que concorriam com Ronald Reagan. Em 1984, tanto a ABC quanto a CBS usaram o vermelho para os Republicanos e o azul para os Democratas. Na virada para os anos 1990, a ABC era a líder de audiência das TVs abertas americanas.

A NBC, criadora do painel de 1976, manteve seu padrão de cores até 1992. Em 1996, ela optou por seguir a concorrência para não confundir os telespectadores.

Foi nos anos 1990 que os jornais impressos americanos começaram a publicar pelo menos algumas de suas páginas coloridas, enquanto o padrão na mídia eletrônica se consolidava.

A divisão se consolidou de vez, porém, no ano 2000. Naquele ano, a eleição foi a mais apertada em décadas, e os mapas com as distinções entre estados “vermelhos” e estados “azuis” passaram horas no ar . Ao longo das semanas seguintes, a recontagem de votos na Flórida reforçou o padrão de cores no imaginário americano.

George W. Bush foi o vencedor depois de o democrata Al Gore admitir a derrota em 13 de dezembro daquele ano, mais de um mês depois do dia da votação.

Comentaristas políticos, títulos de jornais e até comediantes, como David Letterman, começaram a usar os termos “blue states” (estados azuis) e “red states” (estados vermelhos).

Já assimilada pelo público, a divisão se integrou até com o padrão gráfico dos partidos, que passaram a fazer seus logotipos com as respectivas cores.

Atualmente, os estados-chave, onde não há favoritismo claro de um partido, às vezes são chamados de “estados roxos”, ou aparecem em branco nos mapas.

Já candidatos de terceiras vias não têm uma cor definida. O último deles a ganhar eleições em estados e levar delegados ao Colégio Eleitoral foi o então governador do Alabama George Wallace, em 1968, que rompeu com os Democratas para apoiar leis segregacionistas contra negros pelo Partido Independente Americano. Ele conquistou cinco estados.

articles.title: Recorde nos EUA: 17 mulheres vão assumir governos estaduais | G1
articles.standfirst: Com urnas ainda em apuração no Alasca e no Kansas, resultado do pleito de meio de mandato traz vitórias inéditas para mulheres negras, indígenas e estreantes em estados tradicionalmente conservadores.
articles.summary: As eleições midterms nos EUA resultaram em um marco de representatividade feminina, com a eleição das primeiras governadoras negra, indígena e latina no país.
articles.body:
As eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos, chamadas de " midterms ", foram marcadas por uma vitória expressiva do Partido Democrata, que assumiu o controle da Câmara dos Representantes e do Senado. O resultado configura uma mudança de poder em Washington, e Donald Trump terá agora que governar com um Congresso controlado pela oposição.

No centro dessa reconfiguração política, a presença feminina no comando dos estados estabeleceu um recorde histórico : pelo menos 17 mulheres estarão à frente de governos estaduais nos EUA em 2027, superando a marca anterior de 14 governadoras em exercício simultâneo.

15 candidatas conquistaram ou renovaram seus mandatos nas urnas neste ano: 12 são democratas, e 3, republicanas;

Elas somam-se às outras duas governadoras que já cumprem mandatos e não disputaram a eleição este ano.

➡️ Esse número ainda pode aumentar. Até a publicação desta reportagem, os pleitos nos estados do Alasca e do Kansas seguiam em apuração . No Kansas, a democrata Cindy Holscher poderá tornar-se a 16ª governadora eleita nas midterms de 2026.

Entre as governadoras estreantes, 4 se tornaram as primeiras mulheres eleitas para comandar seus estados: Keisha Lance Bottoms , na Geórgia; Marsha Blackburn , no Tennessee; Amy Klobuchar , em Minnesota; e Amy Acton , em Ohio.

Outras três conquistaram marcos relacionados à representatividade:

Deb Haaland, no Novo México, a primeira mulher indígena ;

Deb Haaland foi eleita governadora do Novo México nas midterms de 2026. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Entre as governadoras reeleitas, duas mantiveram marcas históricas: Kathy Hochul , de Nova York, e Maura Healey , de Massachusetts, permanecem como as primeiras a ocupar o cargo nos governos dos estados.

Healey também fez história em 2022 ao se tornar, ao lado de Tina Kotek, do Oregon, uma das duas primeiras mulheres abertamente lésbicas eleitas governadoras nos Estados Unidos.

No Arkansas , a republicana Sarah Huckabee Sanders foi reeleita e continua sendo a primeira mulher a governar o estado. Ela também mantém o posto de governadora mais jovem dos Estados Unidos.

Veja abaixo as eleitas em 2026 para os governos dos estados nos EUA.

Geórgia – Keisha Lance Bottoms (Democrata)

Tennessee – Marsha Blackburn (Republicana)

Rhode Island – Helena Foulkes (Democrata)

Gina Hinojosa será a primera governadora latina de Texas. — Foto: Mike Segar/Reuters via BBC

Massachusetts – Maura Healey (Democrata)

Arkansas – Sarah Huckabee Sanders (Republicana)

New Hampshire – Kelly Ayotte (Republicana)

A governadora Sarah Huckabee Sanders faz o discurso do Estado do Estado em uma sessão conjunta da Assembleia Geral do estado de Arkansas, terça-feira, 14 de janeiro de 2025, no Capitólio estadual de Little Rock, Arkansas, EUA. — Foto: Thomas Metthe/Arkansas Democrat-Gazette via AP.

Governadoras já incumbentes e que não disputaram as midterms: 2

Além das 15 eleitas em novembro de 2026, duas governadoras já haviam assumido os executivos estaduais e continuam com mandatos vigentes:

Virgínia – Abigail Spanberger (Democrata)

Nova Jersey – Mikie Sherrill (Democrata)

Assim como outras lideranças, Spanberger também foi a primeira mulher a ocupar o cargo em seu estado. Já Sherrill foi a primeira veterana das Forças Armadas a se tornar governadora.

Mikie Sherrill, governadora de Nova Jersey. — Foto: Mike Segar/Reuters/Foto de Arquivo

Um século de avanços da liderança feminina nos EUA

A trajetória de mulheres no comando dos estados dos EUA teve seus primeiros passos no início do século XX.

Em 1909, Carolyn B. Shelton atuou como governadora interina do Oregon durante um fim de semana, tornando-se a primeira mulher a exercer o cargo — três anos antes das mulheres do Oregon conquistarem o direito ao voto.

Em 1924, Nellie Tayloe Ross, do Wyoming, foi a primeira mulher eleita governadora no país, empossada em 1925.

Nellie Tayloe Ross, a primeira governadora dos EUA, eleita em 1924 pelo Wyoming. — Foto: Wyoming State Files

articles.body:

Neste dia, não há risco para ocorrências associadas às condições de tempo.

A chuva ainda deve atingir o Norte catarinense entre a madrugada e o início da manhã . Porém, conforme a frente fria se afasta gradativamente de Santa Catarina, as instabilidades começam a perder força e as condições para temporais tendem a cessar.

Com as aberturas de sol , as temperaturas devem voltar a subir, com máximas entre 25°C e 30°C em grande parte do estado e passando dos 30°C em áreas do Litoral Norte e Vale do Itajaí.

As temperaturas mínimas do dia devem ocorrer no período da noite, com valores entre 14°C e 18°C na maioria das regiões, e ficando entre 7°C e 12°C na Serra.

articles.title: Loja de vestidos de festa em SP troca manequins de vitrine após denúncia de racismo  | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeira vitrine tinha figuras negras vestidas com aventais, em posições que simulam servir ou atender manequins brancos que usam vestidos de festa. Depois, loja Arthur Caliman incluiu manequins brancos simulando atendimento. Para Observatório da Branquitude, não basta trocar vitrine, é preciso reconhecer o racismo.
articles.summary: Primeira vitrine tinha figuras negras vestidas com aventais, em posições que simulam servir ou atender manequins brancos que usam vestidos de festa. Depois, loja Arthur Caliman incluiu manequins brancos simulando atendimento. Para Observatório da Branquitude, não basta trocar vitrine, é preciso reconhecer o racismo.
articles.body:
Após reportagem, loja incluiu manequins brancos de aventais servindo outros manequins brancos de vestido de festa — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A loja de vestidos de festa Arthur Caliman, na Avenida Santo Amaro, na Zona Sul de São Paulo, trocou sua vitrine após ser alvo de denúncia de racismo.

Como mostrou o g1 , a disposição dos manequins chamou a atenção por apresentar figuras negras vestidas com aventais, em posições que simulam servir ou atender manequins brancos que usam vestidos de festa.

Na então vitrine, não havia manequins negros usando vestidos de festa, nem manequins brancos representados na função de servir ou atender outros. Com isso, a loja é alvo de uma representação protocolada no Ministério Público de São Paulo (MPSP) na terça-feira (3) e está sendo analisada pela Promotoria de Justiça dos Direitos Humanos – Inclusão Social.

A loja afirmou que após ser contatada pela reportagem, substituiu o manequim da vitrine. Com isso, incluiu dois manequins brancos também simulando um atendimento a mulher branca com vestido de festa.

A Arthur Caliman também afirmou que repudia qualquer forma de racismo e discriminação (leia abaixo).

Para Manuela Thamani, diretora executiva do Observatório da Branquitude, "não basta em 2027 retirar os manequins ou publicar uma nota de desculpas, é preciso que a marca reconheça o racismo e assuma compromissos concretos de mudança."

"O que a vitrine exibiu não é um erro de composição, e sim a materialização de uma hierarquia racial que estrutura a sociedade brasileira desde a escravidão. Corpos brancos aparecem em vestidos de festa, no lugar da celebração, do consumo e do prestígio. Corpos negros aparecem de avental, no lugar da servidão. É a cena colonial reencenada em pleno centro comercial, como se fosse natural."

"Uma vitrine nunca é neutra, existe uma literatura antiga sobre isso desde a semiótica até os profissionais de visual merchandising, e aqui ela está definindo quem é o sujeito do luxo e quem é seu cliente imaginado. Quando uma marca renomada faz essa escolha, ela mobiliza poder simbólico, o poder de dizer, sem precisar dizer em palavras, quem pertence a cada lugar. É isso que chamamos de privilégio simbólico da branquitude: a brancura apresentada como norma, como beleza, como o padrão de humanidade que merece ser servido", afirmou.

"Tem uma intelectual, Grada Kilomba, que nos ajuda a entender esse mecanismo quando mostra que o racismo cotidiano é memória colonial que segue sendo atualizada no presente. A vitrine encena exatamente isso: a branquitude no centro, a negritude como apoio e cenário. Acompanhamos com atenção a representação protocolada no MPSP e esperamos que o caso seja tratado com a seriedade que exige."

O advogado Hédio Silva Jr., fundador do Jusracial, que atua há mais de 28 anos na defesa da igualdade racial e dos direitos das religiões afro-brasileiras, criticou a composição da vitrine.

Para o advogado, a disposição dos manequins transmite uma mensagem que associa pessoas negras a posições de inferioridade social.

"Com base nessa suposta inferioridade genética, são distribuídos lugares sociais. Uma mensagem que induz, incita, encoraja, faz apologia, rigorosamente induz as pessoas a praticarem a discriminação racial. Sem dúvida nenhuma, um crime racial na sua forma mais nua e crua", disse.

"Olha, sem dúvida nenhuma, esta representação, que é mais do que representação, é uma projeção de um lugar de subalternidade da população negra, sempre servindo, subserviente, serviçal de brancos. Ela reproduz um núcleo essencial do racismo, que é a inferioridade, a condição sub-humana que é atribuída à população negra", afirmou.

Manequins na vitrine da loja de vestidos de festa Arthur Caliman alvo de denúncia de racismo — Foto: Paulo Alves/Arquivo pessoal

Vitrine da loja Arthur Caliman — Foto: Paulo Alves/Arquivo pessoal

Em nota, a Arthur Caliman afirmou que a escolha dos manequins das vitrines varia e que, na maioria das vezes, eles são selecionados para valorizar o contraste com a cor das roupas expostas.

Segundo a empresa, foi o que ocorreu na vitrine registrada pela reportagem, que combinou manequins pretos com trajes brancos e um manequim branco com vestido azul-escuro.

A loja também afirmou que a vitrine anterior era composta inteiramente por manequins pretos com vestidos claros.

"Jamais houve a intenção de transmitir qualquer mensagem de cunho racial. Lamentamos o desconforto causado e, assim que recebemos o contato da reportagem, substituímos o manequim da vitrine", declarou.

Vitrine da loja Arthur Caliman com vitrine apontada como racista — Foto: Paulo Alves/arquivo pessoal

articles.summary: Consultas populares em dezenas de estados dos EUA trataram de temas como aborto, direitos de pessoas trans, identificação de eleitores e impostos.
articles.body:
Eleitores de diferentes estados dos Estados Unidos aprovaram medidas para restringir a participação de mulheres e meninas trans em equipes esportivas femininas , enquanto rejeitaram propostas que ampliariam ou restabeleceriam proibições ao aborto.

Os resultados fazem parte de cerca de 150 consultas populares realizadas em mais de 30 estados durante as eleições de meio de mandato, na terça-feira (3).

As propostas, conhecidas como "ballot measures", permitem que a população vote diretamente sobre mudanças nas leis e nas Constituições estaduais . Neste ano, os temas incluíram também regras eleitorais, impostos, justiça criminal e direitos das pessoas trans.

👉 Alguns estados ainda não têm os resultados consolidados e portanto aparecem com "tendência de aprovação" ou "tendência de reprovação".

Pessoas transgênero não podem competir em equipes femininas?

Dia do Orgulho: especialistas explicam importância da terapia afirmativa e como a voz impacta a saúde mental de pessoas trans — Foto: Divulgação

Eleitores do Arizona e de Nebraska aprovaram medidas que restringem a participação de meninas e mulheres trans em equipes esportivas femininas. Em Washington , os primeiros resultados também indicavam apoio à proposta. No Colorado , a apuração apontava maioria favorável a uma medida semelhante.

As propostas ganharam destaque durante a campanha eleitoral. Candidatos republicanos exploraram o tema, depois que estrategistas políticos atribuíram parte da vitória de Donald Trump em 2024 aos ataques do presidente aos direitos das pessoas trans.

Defensores das restrições afirmam que elas protegem meninas e mulheres. Já os críticos argumentam que as medidas discriminam estudantes transgênero.

No Arizona, a proposta amplia uma lei que já impedia meninas e mulheres trans de participar de equipes esportivas de acordo com sua identidade de gênero. Com a mudança, a restrição também passa a valer para escolas particulares .

A medida ainda determina que banheiros e vestiários escolares sejam utilizados apenas por atletas cujo sexo registrado na certidão de nascimento corresponda ao destinado àquelas instalações.

Em Nebraska , os eleitores aprovaram a inclusão da proibição na Constituição estadual, o que torna mais difícil uma eventual reversão da regra pelos parlamentares.

Em Washington , a proposta exige que atletas que queiram integrar equipes femininas tenham o chamado "sexo biológico" verificado por um profissional de saúde. Críticos afirmam que a exigência pode resultar em exames desnecessários e invasivos.

As consultas também trataram de tratamentos médicos de afirmação de gênero para menores de idade.

No Colorado , os primeiros resultados indicavam apoio à proposta que proíbe cirurgias relacionadas à transição de gênero em menores.

No Missouri , por outro lado, os eleitores rejeitaram uma proposta que incluiria na Constituição estadual a proibição desses tratamentos para crianças. O estado já tem uma lei que impede a realização dos procedimentos.

Eleitores de Idaho e Missouri rejeitaram propostas que poderiam ampliar ou restabelecer restrições ao aborto.

Em Idaho, a população votou contra uma iniciativa que estabeleceria o direito ao procedimento até a viabilidade fetal , período geralmente situado em torno da 24ª semana de gestação. O estado proíbe praticamente todos os abortos desde 2022, quando a Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos derrubou a proteção constitucional que garantia o direito em todo o país.

No Missouri, os eleitores também rejeitaram uma proposta que restabeleceria a proibição do aborto, dois anos depois de terem aprovado uma medida para derrubar essa restrição.

Diferentemente da consulta de 2024, que partiu de uma iniciativa popular, a proposta deste ano foi apresentada pelo Legislativo estadual, controlado pelos republicanos. O texto também previa a proibição de tratamentos médicos de afirmação de gênero para menores de idade.

Eleitores da Califórnia e do Colorado rejeitaram propostas que exigiriam informações adicionais de identificação para votar pelo correio. A medida previa a apresentação dos quatro últimos números de um documento oficial, como o número do Seguro Social — equivalente à identificação previdenciária americana — ou da carteira de motorista.

Em Nevada , os eleitores apoiaram uma proposta semelhante.

No Arizona , os primeiros resultados indicavam que a população também rejeitaria uma medida que exigiria documento com foto para votar pelo correio. A apuração ainda não havia sido concluída na manhã de quarta-feira (4).

O texto da proposta, no entanto, não especificava como a exigência seria aplicada.

Votação das midterms no Maine, EUA — Foto: ANGELA WEISS/AFP

Eleitores do Missouri rejeitaram um novo mapa eleitoral elaborado por republicanos que dividiria um dos dois distritos do estado com tendência democrata. Em Maryland , por outro lado, a população aprovou uma mudança constitucional que facilitará o redesenho dos distritos pelos parlamentares.

A disputa faz parte de uma ofensiva republicana liderada por Donald Trump desde 2025 para redesenhar os mapas eleitorais em diferentes estados e transformar distritos controlados por democratas em áreas com maior possibilidade de vitória republicana.

O tema deve continuar no centro da disputa política até 2028 .

No Missouri, a Justiça havia determinado que o novo mapa só poderia entrar em vigor se fosse aprovado pelos eleitores. A proposta acabou rejeitada.

Em Maryland , a mudança aprovada abre caminho para que o Legislativo estadual, controlado pelos democratas, elimine, em 2028, o único distrito do estado com tendência republicana.

Na Califórnia , a proposta que criaria o primeiro imposto sobre bilionários do mundo caminhava para ser rejeitada na manhã de quarta-feira (4).

A chamada Proposição 40 previa uma cobrança única de 5% sobre o patrimônio mundial de cada um dos cerca de 250 bilionários residentes no estado.

Apesar do apoio popular à tributação dos mais ricos, especialmente entre os democratas, a proposta dividiu o partido na Califórnia. O governador Gavin Newsom, apontado como possível candidato à Presidência em 2028, se opôs à medida.

Ele alertou que a cobrança poderia levar empresas de tecnologia bem-sucedidas a transferir suas operações para outros estados.

Em Montana , os eleitores aprovaram uma proposta para proibir que empresas gastem dinheiro em campanhas eleitorais. A medida busca contornar uma decisão histórica da Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos, de 2010, conhecida como Citizens United.

Na ocasião, a Corte decidiu que empresas e sindicatos têm direito constitucional de gastar quantias ilimitadas em campanhas, desde que atuem de forma independente dos candidatos.

A decisão abriu caminho para a criação dos chamados super PACs , organizações que arrecadam e gastam grandes quantias para influenciar eleições, e de grupos conhecidos como dark money , que não precisam divulgar a identidade de seus financiadores.

No Alasca , os primeiros resultados apontavam uma pequena vantagem para a manutenção do sistema eleitoral conhecido como voto por escolha ranqueada .

Nesse modelo, os eleitores classificam os candidatos em ordem de preferência. Se nenhum deles alcançar mais de 50% dos votos, o menos votado é eliminado , e seus votos são transferidos para a segunda opção indicada pelos eleitores. O processo se repete até que um candidato alcance a maioria.

O sistema ganhou destaque neste ano por causa da disputa acirrada por uma vaga no Senado entre o republicano Dan Sullivan , que tenta a reeleição, e a democrata Mary Peltola . Outro candidato republicano na mesma cédula também tem o nome de Dan Sullivan.

O jornal The New York Times informou que integrantes da equipe de Peltola trabalharam com advogados da campanha e funcionários graduados do braço de campanha dos democratas no Senado para recrutar o outro Dan Sullivan, um professor aposentado. A Reuters afirmou que não conseguiu verificar a informação.

No Alabama , os eleitores aprovaram uma proposta que obrigará as escolas a tocar a primeira estrofe do hino nacional pelo menos uma vez por semana.

articles.standfirst: Jacobo Bucaram é procurado pelos EUA e pode ser extraditado.
articles.summary: Jacobo Bucaram é procurado pelos EUA e pode ser extraditado.
articles.body:
Jacobo Bucaram Pulley preso em Guayaquil. — Foto: John Reimberg/X

Um dos filhos do ex-presidente do Equador Abdalá Bucaram e outras quatro pessoas foram presos por suspeita de ligação com o narcotráfico, em uma operação regional que contou com a colaboração da DEA (agência antidrogas), informou nesta quarta-feira (4) o ministro do Interior John Reimberg.

Jacobo Bucaram Pulley, filho do ex-presidente, foi detido na cidade de Guayaquil, juntamente com duas pessoas. Outros dois envolvidos foram presos no Panamá.

"Os cinco cidadãos receberam uma notificação vermelha da Interpol e são requeridos por autoridades dos Estados Unidos por supostos crimes relacionados ao narcotráfico", publicou Reimberg no X.

A ação permitiu "colocar os detidos à disposição das autoridades competentes, no âmbito dos respectivos processos de extradição para os Estados Unidos".

Abdalá Bucaram criticou as acusações contra seu filho e atribuiu a prisão dele ao "ódio político", conforme mensagem publicada no X. Em 2022, Washington declarou o ex-presidente, sua mulher e três filhos do casal inelegíveis para entrar nos Estados Unidos, por "participação em atos significativos de corrupção".

articles.title: After seismic shift in US, a new Congress but an old consensus
articles.summary: The shift in US Congressional control is a pivotal moment for Washington, but its impact on the India–US strategic partnership will likely be more subtle
articles.body: The shift in US Congressional control is a pivotal moment for Washington, but its impact on the India–US strategic partnership will likely be more subtle than disruptive. With President Donald Trump retaining executive control though over US foreign policy, India will need to guard against any further complication of the West Asia conflict.The relationship rests on bipartisan support and consensus built around Indo-Pacific cooperation amid Chinese assertiveness, along with people-to-people contacts and technology and defence ties. Electoral cycles have done little to deter this momentum built over the past 25 years.However, despite this core alignment, the strategic partnership also hit its lowest ebb in decades under the second Trump administration over issues like asymmetrical trade demands, India's reluctance to abandon its energy ties with Russia, US immigration policies and also Washington's Pakistan outreach leading effectively to the re-hyphenation of its approach to the region.To what extent a tighter Congressional scrutiny of Trump's actions – including on issues related to Iran and Ukraine – can constrain his foreign policy is unclear, as the legislative turnaround is unlikely to dent his broad executive authority over US diplomacy and military even in the face of a domestic pushback.Significantly, the ASEAN summit this month in Manila – where PM Narendra Modi will be present – might indicate how the midterm results could reshape Trump's approach to global affairs. Of immediate interest not just for India but also Japan and Australia will be the Quad leaders' summit which is scheduled for November 16 on the margins of ASEAN. Modi may have also have a bilateral meeting with Trump.It was India's turn to host the leaders' summit for the past 2 years but Trump's apparent reluctance to travel to New Delhi amid bilateral trade discord delayed the event, leading many to conclude that the president had downgraded Quad to pursue closer ties with Beijing.Preserving Quad for a free and open Indo-Pacific is a key foreign policy priority for India and Japan. The leaders' summit in Manila will be of particular significance as it will take place in the middle of the Philippines' continued maritime tensions with Beijing, and days before Trump's visit to China for the APEC leaders' meeting.Strategic ties in the form of Quad, defence cooperation and initiatives like TRUST (formerly iCET) on critical and emerging technology will continue to deepen, based on the bipartisan foundation. As it negotiates its own trade agreement with the US, India will watch out though for potential legislative hurdles over labour and environmental standards.A Democratic majority could also seek to curb the Trump administration's unilateral tariff actions, ensuring some reprieve for India. It could also offer a check against restrictive immigration legislation, providing relief potentially for high-skilled Indian professionals and H-1B visa holders. Democrats have traditionally been more vocal or even critical of India on human rights and other internal issues, but this has rarely been a deal-breaker.After the midterm outcomes, India will look to balance its engagement with the White House by cultivating ties with key Democratic committee chairs. According to Indian officials, the relationship based on similar values and strategic goals will continue to grow."American funding, research, and businesses pair perfectly with India's talent, large workforce, and ambition. Above all, the close connection between regular people, especially the active Indian-American community, keeps this partnership strong, reliable, and focused on the future," said a source, who spoke on condition of anonymity.You use AI every day. articles.title: A woman began restoring and gifting American Girl dolls in 2012; her volunteer-run charity has now delivered more than 3,000 kits to children
articles.summary: Susan Robison started restoring and gifting American Girl dolls in 2012 after witnessing how a cherished toy could give a child a sense of safety and
articles.body: Susan Robison started restoring and gifting American Girl dolls in 2012 after witnessing how a cherished toy could give a child a sense of safety and belonging. What began as a small operation from her home has grown into Special DOLLivery, a volunteer-powered nonprofit that provides restored dolls and complete accessory kits to children in vulnerable homes. Fourteen years later, the organisation has delivered more than 3,000 doll kits, bringing comfort and companionship to children who might otherwise go without one. Its work relies entirely on volunteers, donated supplies and community support, according to the charity's website.Susan Robison founded Special DOLLivery after seeing the comfort a doll could bringRobison founded Special DOLLivery in 2012 after witnessing firsthand how a cherished doll could influence a child's sense of security and belonging. A former foster care advocate and lifelong crafter, she began restoring dolls from her home and giving them to children who needed companionship. The one-woman operation gradually developed into a community-supported charitable initiative. Robison's experience working with children in foster care helped shape the organisation's mission of using dolls to provide comfort and encourage imaginative play. Special DOLLivery describes her service as the foundation of its work.American Girl doll kits include restored toys, clothes and booksEach Special DOLLivery kit contains a fully restored 18-inch American Girl doll dressed in a special outfit, along with 10 additional outfits, pyjamas, doll bedding, a chapter book and a carrying bag. Volunteers assemble the packages by collecting gently used dolls, cleaning and restoring them, and preparing the accompanying accessories. The organisation aims to give each recipient more than a second-hand toy by providing a complete collection that children can use to create stories and develop imaginative play. Its website describes the kits as carefully hand-assembled gifts intended to make children feel valued.Volunteer-run charity has delivered more than 3,000 doll kits since 2012Special reports state that it has delivered more than 3,000 doll kits since its founding, with 233 deliveries recorded in 2026 on its homepage. The organisation is entirely volunteer-powered, with donations and community participation supporting its operations. Individuals and families can contribute gently used dolls, clothing and supplies, shop through its wish list or attend packing events. Companies can also sponsor delivery events and organise group packing sessions. The charity's founder page separately reports more than 4,000 dolls delivered across Utah, although this figure differs from the homepage's total for doll kits.Susan Robison receives recognition for her service to childrenRobison's work has also received recognition in Utah. She was named a 2025 Governor's Spirit of Service honoree, following earlier recognition as a Layton City Hometown Hero in 2024 and a Country Life Great List winner in 2021. Her approach centres on the belief that dolls can help children imagine positive futures through play. Special DOLLivery continues to invite individuals, families and businesses to contribute to its mission through donations, volunteering and sponsorships. articles.summary: SURAT: Beheaded and dumped in two different locations, a textile worker's body was found in a cemetery in Surat, while his severed head was recovered near
articles.body: SURAT: Beheaded and dumped in two different locations, a textile worker's body was found in a cemetery in Surat, while his severed head was recovered near railway tracks beneath the Alkapuri bridge in Katargam.Police have arrested his 54-year-old co-worker, who allegedly killed him over a seven-month salary dispute.The accused, identified as Sachitra Bal, a textile worker from Odisha, allegedly murdered Sanjay Khosla, with whom he worked at the same textile unit.Dispute over Rs 30,000 in alleged salary deductionsAccording to police, Khosla maintained records of the working hours of all employees at the textile unit. Since Khosla earned more than Bal, the latter suspected that he was deducting money from his wages and pocketing it.Bal believed Khosla’s records had cost him Rs 160 daily for seven months, amounting to a loss of around Rs 30,000. The alleged deductions led to repeated quarrels between the two and strained their relationship.On November 1, Bal allegedly took Khosla to his residence in Rail Rahat Colony, Katargam, on some pretext. During the afternoon, he attacked the victim's neck with a sharp-edged weapon, killing him.After the murder, Bal allegedly stuffed the body into a sack and, late at night, dumped it in CNI cemetery near his residence after breaking a section of its boundary wall.In an attempt to conceal the victim’s identity, the accused allegedly returned to the spot early on November 3 and severed the head from the body. He then dumped it near the railway tracks beneath the Alkapuri bridge, around 3km away.Police crack case, recover severed headAfter discovering the beheaded body, Katargam police launched an investigation and traced the murder to Bal. He reportedly confessed to the crime and disclosed where he had disposed of the head.Police subsequently recovered the head from near the railway tracks.Katargam police registered an FIR under relevant provisions of the BNS and Arms Act. articles.title: 'I have become psycho': After beheading wife, man sits in temple with severed head; what he told cops
articles.summary: KOLKATA: A man allegedly beheaded his wife and sat inside a Kali temple with her severed head resting on his lap, while their two sons sat beside him, in
articles.body: KOLKATA: A man allegedly beheaded his wife and sat inside a Kali temple with her severed head resting on his lap, while their two sons sat beside him, in West Bengal's South Dinajpur district on Wednesday.The accused, Rintu Ghosh, a former bus conductor, was found inside the temple in Ward 4 of Narayanpur, under Gangarampur, with a knife in his hand and his wife's severed head on his lap.The incident came to light after local residents spotted Ghosh inside the temple and alerted the police. The victim, identified as 35-year-old Seema Sarkar, had allegedly been killed before the accused brought her severed head to the temple.Accused links actions to loss of jobA police team led by Gangarampur police station inspector-in-charge Purnendu Kundu reached the spot and arrested Ghosh. Police recovered the woman's body and sent it for post-mortem examination.While being taken away in a police van, Ghosh spoke to reporters about losing his job with the North Bengal State Transport Corporation (NBSTC). He said, "After losing my job from NBSTC and going to the police station, I have become a psycho."Relative points to changes in his behaviourAccording to a relative, Rajesh Pramanik, Ghosh had been struggling to make ends meet after losing his job as a bus conductor. He later tried his hand at small business activities but failed to find a stable source of income.Pramanik also claimed that Ghosh's lifestyle had changed in recent times. He had reportedly given up non-vegetarian food and turned vegetarian, while also displaying behaviour that the relative described as tantric.Police question accused to establish motivePolice are interrogating Ghosh to determine what led to the alleged murder. articles.title: Madonna's charity has reached more than 500,000 children in Malawi over 20 years; its work extends beyond hospitals to free education and the arts
articles.summary: Madonna's commitment to improving children's lives in Malawi has grown into a two-decade effort supporting healthcare, education and creative
articles.body: Madonna's commitment to improving children's lives in Malawi has grown into a two-decade effort supporting healthcare, education and creative opportunities across the country. Through Raising Malawi, the charity she co-founded in 2006, more than 500,000 children have been reached through programmes designed to address some of the challenges facing young people and their families. While its work includes specialised medical care, the organisation has also invested in free schooling and arts education, recognising that children need opportunities to learn, develop their talents and build better futures.Madonna's Raising Malawi charity has reached more than 500,000 childrenMadonna founded Raising Malawi in 2006 following trips to Malawi that exposed the hardships children face, especially those without access to education and healthcare. The singer co-founded the charity which works with communities in Malawi, helping children through healthcare, education and community programmes, according to the charity’s official website.Over the last 20 years, its work has touched the lives of more than 500,000 children. The organisation says its approach extends beyond immediate aid, backing services and opportunities that can have a lasting effect on children’s lives.It currently runs three programme areas: healthcare, education and the arts. These initiatives include specialist medical treatment, free schooling, vocational opportunities, college scholarships and regular creative classes. They together represent an approach that has regard to children’s physical well-being, learning and personal development.What changed with the Mercy James Centre's specialist medical careHealthcare has been one of Raising Malawi's most visible areas of work. Its flagship facility, the Mercy James Centre, is located within Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital in Blantyre. The centre provides specialised treatment for children who need surgery and intensive care, services that are particularly important in a country where access to specialist paediatric healthcare has been limited.According to Raising Malawi, the centre is the only hospital in Malawi dedicated to paediatric surgery and intensive care. It is also run with Malawian medical professionals at its heart, with a focus on developing local expertise so that the country can continue providing specialist treatment in the future.The organisation's website highlights the role of medical director Dr Eric Borgstein, who returned to Malawi in 1992 after training in Scotland and the Netherlands. For many years, he was the country's only paediatric surgeon. He established a national training programme that increased the number of paediatric surgery specialists from one in 2010 to six by 2022. The centre opened in 2017, creating an important base for treatment and professional training.A March 2025 report by Digital Journal also highlighted the centre's wider contribution. It reported that the Mercy James Institute for Pediatric Surgery and Intensive Care provides life-saving operations to around 2,000 children annually and helps train healthcare workers in paediatric surgery and intensive care.The report also covered a fundraising event held by Madonna on March 11, 2025, at Diane von Furstenberg's headquarters in New York. Hosted by comedian Amy Schumer, the gathering marked the launch of renewed initiatives supporting Raising Malawi's work. Madonna's daughter Mercy James performed on the piano, while guests including Chris Rock and Lauren Sanchez attended.Free education opened doors for children in rural communitiesAlongside healthcare, Raising Malawi has supported efforts to make education more accessible, particularly for children living in communities where reaching a school can be difficult.One of its notable education partnerships was with the international non-profit organisation buildOn. In a December 2012 update, buildOn reported that it had worked with Madonna and Raising Malawi to construct 10 schools in villages selected because they needed better educational facilities. The partners had originally planned to complete the buildings within 18 months but finished the project in just 12 months.The new schools addressed practical problems that had prevented children from attending classes regularly. Some pupils previously had to walk long distances to reach schools in neighbouring villages, while others studied outdoors under trees or in basic structures with thatched roofs. The new buildings provided proper classrooms where lessons could continue during rainy weather.By December 2012, 6 of the 10 schools were already being used. The project was expected to benefit nearly 5,000 children.Gender equality was another important part of the initiative. The partners aimed to ensure that girls attended in equal numbers to boys. Madonna also highlighted the significance of this commitment, particularly in communities where educational opportunities for girls remained limited. More than half of the pupils expected to attend the new schools were girls.The buildOn report also described how the construction projects brought communities together. At Mkoma Chilolo, local residents worked collectively to build the school, with community leaders viewing the facility as an opportunity to encourage enrolment and reduce illiteracy.Why the arts have become part of the charity's missionRaising Malawi's work also recognises that education is not limited to traditional classroom subjects. The organisation supports the arts through the Jacaranda School for Orphans, where children receive regular music and visual-art lessons alongside their academic education.According to the charity's website, the school provides free education from preschool through secondary level, with additional vocational training and college scholarships. Its arts programme gives pupils opportunities to develop creative skills and perform on stages in Malawi and internationally.The importance of this work is also reflected in Malawi's wider music community. Malawi Tourism reported on the British singer-songwriter Annemarie Quinn, who moved to Blantyre in 2016 and was the Arts Programmes Director at the Jacaranda School for Orphans in partnership with Raising Malawi.Over four years Quinn has worked with more than 40 Malawian musicians to produce an album called Blue Sky Thinking. Artists such as Faith Mussa, Lazarus and the Jacaranda School for Orphans choir were involved in the project. It included traditional instruments, locally made musical objects and recordings influenced by Malawi’s cultural environment.A wider network of support for vulnerable childrenRaising Malawi’s work goes beyond its three core programme areas. Other organisations and initiatives backed by the charity included the Jacaranda School for Orphans, Home of Hope Children's Homes and Ascent Soccer, reported Digital Journal.Ascent Soccer focuses on giving young Malawian athletes opportunities to develop, adding sport to the organisation's wider interest in children's development.Madonna's continued involvement, including the renewed fundraising initiative announced in 2025, is intended to help sustain these programmes.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ladakh becomes India's first 100% organic Union Territory; 4 places to experience its traditional food culture
articles.summary: Ladakh is better known for its massive rugged landscapes, pristine high-altitude lakes and sight of the universe beyond Earth in its dark sky reserves.
articles.body: Ladakh is better known for its massive rugged landscapes, pristine high-altitude lakes and sight of the universe beyond Earth in its dark sky reserves. The religious and literary culture of Ladakh is enriched by the virtue of its location being at the intersection of Indian, Central Asian and Tibetan-Chinese cultures. However, the remoteness of the Union Territory has led to the establishment of its own food practices. Thus, innovation and their consideration towards sustainability has led Ladakh to becoming India's first 100% organic Union Territory. It was declared by Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena on October 25, 2026.In organic farming, there is a focus on chemical-free farming which is attractive in the global markets, providing farmers better market opportunities and boosting their incomes. According to the Organic Research Centre, global retail sales of organic food and drink rose to 145.0 billion euros in 2024. The aim is to provide individual organic certification to farmers as it will increase their exposure to the international markets. Organic farming is an approach towards sustainable agriculture with a focus to protect soil and water resources.Ladakhi food is special not just for its taste but for the innovative use of the limited ingredients. In a landscape where farming seasons are short, winters are long and harsh; agricultural innovation helps in bringing life to the table. Barley and buckwheat are staples and wild herbs lend their distinctive flavours to everyday cooking. Apricots are celebrated annually at the festival during its blooming season. The Ladakhi cuisine also reflects centuries of cultural exchange along old trade routes, particularly in the villages closer to Baltistan. Here’s guide to have the most authentic experience of food of Ladakh.Alchi Kitchen, AlchiThe village is about 70 km from Leh and is known for its ancient monastery. At Alchi Kitchen, local women of Ladakh bring the traditional food with locally sourced ingredients on the table. The menu includes khambir, a thick, round, whole-wheat bread with a chewy centre and a rustic crust. It is a staple in Ladakhi households, often eaten with butter, eggs or other accompaniments. Then try sky u (also spelt skyu), a comforting stew of handmade dough pieces and vegetables, or mok mok, the local take on dumplings.What to try: Khambir, skyu and seasonal apricot-based dishes.Why go: This is a good place to discover Ladakhi food beyond the familiar restaurant staples and see how a local kitchen keeps culinary traditions alive.The Jade House, LehTheir much-talked-about Artisanal Alchemy breakfast brings Ladakhi ingredients into a thoughtfully prepared, multi-course meal. Apricots are especially worth paying attention to. In Ladakh, these golden fruits are more than a photogenic orchard crop: they are eaten fresh in season, dried for later use and transformed into preserves and other preparations. Barley, meanwhile, has long been central to local food traditions, including tsampa, roasted barley flour that can be mixed into drinks or eaten in other forms.What to try: Ask whether an artisanal breakfast or a seasonal local-produce meal is available during your stay.Why go: For a closer look at how Ladakhi ingredients can move from a family kitchen and orchard to a carefully curated dining experience.The Balti Farm, TurtukTurtuk is a village in the Nubra region near the India-Pakistan border. The farm is shaped by the history and culture of Baltistan which lies right across the Line of Control (LoC). It offers a classic farm to table experience with dishes such as ba-leh, barley noodles served in lamb broth with local herbs, and kisir, buckwheat pancakes served with a yoghurt relish. Another regional bread, bringa, is made with buckwheat and traditionally enjoyed with butter. Barley and buckwheat are the major organic farming crops grown in the region due to their resistance to the cold and dry climate.What to try: Kisir, bringa and Balti dishes featuring barley, herbs and seasonal produce.Why go: For a culinary experience that takes you beyond Leh and into the distinctive food traditions of a historic Himalayan borderland.Tsas by Dholkar, LehNestled among apple and apricot orchards at Dolkhar, on Lower Tukcha Road in Leh, Tsas takes its name from the Ladakhi word for “kitchen garden”. The plant-based restaurant builds its menu around produce grown in its own garden and ingredients sourced from local producers, bringing a contemporary twist to Ladakh’s culinary heritage. Expect inventive dishes such as ramen infused with Himalayan herbs, hand-rolled pasta with yak cheese, and a burnt-lime thenthuk alongside traditional Ladakhi noodle soup, namthuk. Its seven-course chef’s tasting menu offers an even deeper exploration of regional ingredients, with creations featuring sun-dried apricots, local labo cheese and nakshan (black peas). At Tsas, the idea is not simply to serve local food, but to reinterpret Ladakh’s seasonal harvest through thoughtful, modern cooking.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: American singer Tony Bennett's daughters say they received only $245,000 each from his estate; they are accusing their brother of taking millions through commissions and trust transactions
articles.summary: The daughters of late American singer Tony Bennett say they received just $245,000 each from their father’s estate, accusing their brother, D’Andrea
articles.body: The daughters of late American singer Tony Bennett say they received just $245,000 each from their father’s estate, accusing their brother, D’Andrea “Danny” Bennett, of taking millions through excessive commissions, financial deals and trust transactions. Antonia and Johanna Bennett allege that their brother used his control over their father’s finances to enrich himself before and after the singer’s death in 2023. In a lawsuit filed in New York, the sisters also question the sale of their father’s music catalogue and image rights shortly before his death. They are seeking damages and Danny’s removal as head of the family trust.How did Danny Bennett allegedly misuse his father’s estateAccording to the lawsuit, Danny Bennett exercised control over Tony Bennett’s financial affairs both before and after his death through several positions of authority. These included serving as his personal and professional manager, holding power of attorney, managing his company Benedetto Arts and acting as trustee of the family trust.The sisters allege that their brother breached his fiduciary duties through what the lawsuit describes as “self-interested and conflicted transactions, excessive and unearned commissions”. They also accuse him of arranging substantial loans and gifts for himself and his children. According to the filing, these transactions reduced the assets available for distribution under their father’s will.What does the lawsuit allege about Tony’s Alzheimer’s and financesAccording to AP news, the lawsuit also alleges that Danny Bennett took advantage of his father’s diminished capacity in the later stages of his life due to Alzheimer’s disease. The sisters claim he arranged financial deals that generated millions of dollars for himself and his company.One of the transactions highlighted in the lawsuit involved the sale of Tony Bennett’s music catalogue, along with the rights to his name, likeness and image. The deal with brand development firm Iconoclast took place shortly before the singer’s death, according to the filing. The sisters allege that the transaction was among the arrangements through which their brother financially benefited.Antonia and Johanna say they have received a “single modest distribution” of $245,000 each from the estate. They argue that the amount is “nowhere close” to what they believe they are entitled to under their father’s will, which provides for his four children to share his assets equally. The lawsuit seeks damages, with the amount to be determined at trial.What does the lawsuit allege about Tony Bennett’s belongingsThe latest legal action follows a lawsuit the sisters filed against their brother in June 2024, seeking an accounting of their father’s assets and raising concerns about how the estate had been managed. The new complaint goes further, accusing Danny Bennett of breaching his fiduciary responsibilities and seeking his removal as trustee of the family trust.The sisters have also accused their brother of disposing of belongings with significant sentimental value to them in what they describe as a malicious and retaliatory manner. The complaint says their attempts to obtain financial information through the earlier lawsuit were followed by disputes over access to their father’s possessions. Antonia Bennett also claimed that a piano her father had promised her was in terrible condition when the sisters were eventually allowed to tour his apartment. They alleged that they were denied access to much of the property.How has Danny Bennett responded to his sisters’ allegationsDanny Bennett has rejected the accusations through a spokesperson, describing the latest lawsuit as another attempt to misrepresent their father’s wishes. The statement said: “Danny has followed his father’s plans with integrity and care,” adding that the allegations against him were unsubstantiated.The spokesperson also maintained that Tony and Danny Bennett had a record of unprecedented success together and said Danny remained committed to preserving his father’s memory and legacy. Tony Bennett died in 2023 at the age of 96. He had been diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease in 2016, although no specific cause of death was given.Tony Bennett was one of the most recognised interpreters of classic American songs, best known for recordings including I Left My Heart in San Francisco. During his career, he released more than 70 albums, won 19 Grammy Awards and received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. The legal dispute between his daughters and brother concerns the management and distribution of the singer’s estate following his death.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Respect seniors, end BJP-RSS hatred': Rijiju's seven-point advice to Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday took a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, listing seven conditions that he said the
articles.body: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday took a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, listing seven conditions that he said the opposition party should follow if it wants to "win more MPs".In a post on X, Rijiju said Gandhi should spend more time in India, avoid meeting people he described as "anti-India" and stop promoting their agenda. He also urged the Congress leader to respect senior leaders and learn from their experience, saying it was part of Indian tradition.Listing the conditions, Rijiju asked Gandhi to "spend more time in India and avoid secret foreign vacations frequently."He further advised him to "end deep hatred against BJP, RSS and Modi Ji" and "treat BJP as political opponent, not enemy."The minister also asked Gandhi to take "Parliament more seriously" and allow MPs to participate in debates and discussions."Respect Constitution of India, and honour Constitutional Institutions, and allow Congress party to function as a democratic party and smash dynastic politics," he said, listing the final two conditions.Rijiju's remarks came amid an ongoing exchange between the ruling BJP and the Congress over Rahul Gandhi's demand for an open debate with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Earlier on Wednesday, Rijiju shared a video clip of his speech in Parliament during which opposition leaders had walked out of the House."Parliament is the House for debates & discussion. But people who don't believe in democracy, debates and discussion are talking about debate," the parliamentary affairs minister said.Meanwhile, Rahul renewed his challenge to Modi for an open debate, claiming that he could establish within five minutes that the prime minister was a traitor. His remarks drew a sharp response from Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.Following Rahul's challenge, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also urged the prime minister to come forward and answer questions raised over alleged vote theft.In a post on X, Kharge said Modi had no answers on the "vote chori" issue and should accept Gandhi's challenge to debate various subjects, including "foreign connections"."You don't come to Parliament. You have not done a SINGLE OPEN PRESS CONFERENCE; it's time you came for a DEBATE.“Come forward, Face Questions. Tell the Nation why did you indulge in VOTE CHORI !!” Kharge said.“PM Modi is parroting his flop line of ‘Dimaagi Naxal’! He has NO answer on Vote Chori and the Open Challenge by Rahul Gandhi to discuss how he mortgaged Indian interests to Foreign powers!” he added.Kharge also questioned Home Minister Amit Shah's remarks about three crore voters being "ghuspaithiyas" (infiltrators), asking what he had been doing as home minister if illegal immigrants had entered the country.“He should be sacked for his incompetence,” the Congress president said.Responding to Rahul's challenge, Sitharaman said Parliament was already an appropriate venue for a debate and reminded him that he was the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha."Rahul ji, you ask the Prime Minister to choose a venue for a debate. There is already one: Parliament, where you happen to be the LoP."Just yesterday, Home Minister Shri Amit Shah offered a special session to debate SIR and EVMs. Why not show the same enthusiasm for a debate in Parliament that you show while issuing challenges on social media?" Sitharaman said on X.She said that demanding answers also required Rahul to stay and hear the government's response."Demanding answers also carries an obligation to hear them," she said, alleging that Gandhi and other Congress leaders had walked out of Parliament on several occasions while the government was responding to their allegations.Sitharaman also accused the Congress and its INDIA bloc allies of repeatedly disrupting parliamentary proceedings, resulting in entire sittings being washed out.She further questioned the nature of Gandhi's allegations and asked him to present specific claims backed by evidence."Simply throwing together a long list of accusations doesn’t make your case any stronger. As LoP, you are expected to show some seriousness and responsibility."You say, 'Daro mat'. Then bring the facts, face the scrutiny and stay to hear the answers. In the House, uphold the standards of debate you demand from others," she said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell and her husband, Robert, plan to distribute more than 2 million shares to eligible American children, with the first allocation expected in December 2026
articles.summary: SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell and her husband, Robert, are moving ahead with a pledge of more than 2 million shares in the space company for American
articles.body: SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell and her husband, Robert, are moving ahead with a pledge of more than 2 million shares in the space company for American children's investment accounts under President Donald Trump's federal programme. The first distributions are expected by the end of 2026, with children aged 11 to 17 in lower-income communities among the intended beneficiaries. In an announcement shared on 30 October, Shotwell outlined the eligibility criteria, including children living in ZIP code areas with median family incomes of $57,000 or less. The planned contribution will also extend to other groups, including children in foster care and military families stationed overseas.Gwynne Shotwell's pledge of more than 2 million SpaceX sharesShotwell's announcement concerns a gift made by her and her husband rather than a donation being presented as a corporate contribution from SpaceX itself. The couple's commitment involves more than two million shares in SpaceX, which are being moved into escrow ahead of their planned distribution through children's investment accounts. At the time, she indicated that she wanted to direct a significant portion of her SpaceX holdings towards children, with particular attention to families living in areas with lower incomes. The new details establish the broad eligibility criteria and provide December as the expected distribution period.Trump Account eligibility for children aged 11 to 17 in low-income ZIP codesAccording to Shotwell's announcement on X (Formerly Twitter), the first allocation is aimed at American children aged between 11 and 17 who live in ZIP code areas where median family income is $57,000 or below. The geographical approach means eligibility is assessed using income information associated with a residential area, rather than relying solely on an individual family's reported earnings.There is also provision for communities where the population is too small for the US census to publish a reliable median family income figure. Children in these locations are included in the initial eligibility group, avoiding a situation in which families in sparsely populated areas are automatically excluded because comparable census information is unavailable. The shares are expected to reach the relevant accounts in December, once the administrative and transfer arrangements have been completed.Shotwell's additional contribution to benefit eligible Texas childrenShotwell also outlined a further contribution expected to be finalised in the weeks following her announcement. This stage is intended to extend support to children in military families stationed overseas and those living in foster care. The proposed eligibility threshold for these children is a family income of $90,000 or less, with the relevant ZIP codes located in counties close to the Shotwell family's home in Texas.This second stage introduces a different geographical and social emphasis. While the first allocation is primarily organised around lower-income communities across the country, the subsequent contribution includes specific provisions for children whose family circumstances or living arrangements might otherwise make participation more complicated.The announcement did not provide a final distribution schedule for this additional group.How the Trump Accounts fit into the arrangementTrump Accounts are a US federal initiative designed to give children access to investment savings at an early age. Rather than functioning as ordinary bank savings accounts, they are intended to hold investments that can potentially grow over a longer period.The programme has attracted contributions and public attention from several prominent business figures. Its structure has also created opportunities for private donors to direct financial assets towards children's accounts, bringing company shares into discussions about how young people might build financial resources before adulthood.Government agencies and financial partners involvedShotwell acknowledged the organisations involved in preparing the contribution, including SpaceX, the US Treasury Department and the Internal Revenue Service. The Dell Foundation, Greater Horizons and Invest America were also among the organisations she thanked.Two legal firms, Morgan Lewis and Gibson Dunn, were credited for their work on the arrangements. Their involvement reflects the administrative and legal considerations associated with transferring a large block of company shares into accounts intended for individual beneficiaries.Shotwell also recognised Brad Gerstner and Michael Dell for their contributions to the wider effort.What the pledge means for SpaceX stock and children's savingsThe contribution places SpaceX equity directly within a programme intended to give young Americans an early connection to investing. For recipients, the potential benefit will depend on the value of the shares over time, as well as the rules governing when and how the assets can be accessed.For now, the immediate focus is the December transfer. More than two million SpaceX shares are being prepared for distribution, with the first group centred on teenagers in lower-income and data-limited ZIP code areas. A second allocation is expected to bring military families overseas, children in foster care and additional Texas teenagers into the arrangement.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 1989, New York paved two test roads with ground-up tyre rubber; after 3 years, the state transport department judged neither project economical nor successful
articles.summary: In 1989, New York paved two test roads using ground-up tyre rubber, hoping to reduce waste and improve road longevity. After three years, the state found the project neither economical nor successful, echoing sentiments from other states involved in similar initiatives.
articles.body: Turning old tyres into roads sounds like a win-win situation. It would cut waste, and roads could last longer. New York tried that idea in 1989. The state paved two test roads with ground-up tyre rubber in the asphalt, according to a Federal Highway Administration guide on waste materials in pavement construction. Three years later, the state transportation department said neither project was economical nor successful.Why New York ran the test In 1987, state lawmakers instructed the transportation department to carry out a pilot project involving recycled tyre rubber on state roads. This is explained in the progress report of the New York State Department of Transportation covering the first three years after the roads were built. The project resulted in the construction of two experimental roads during the summer of 1989. Each road had five test sections. Each test section was 2,000 feet long. Three sections had 1%, 2%, or 3% rubber by weight of the mixture. One section used a branded additive with larger pieces of rubber. The other had a standard mix kept for comparison. Both roads used what engineers called the dry process. In this particular process, ground rubber replaces a part of the fine aggregate in the mixture. The federal guide notes the most common US version came from Sweden in the late 1960s. It was sold in the US under the trade name PlusRide. The New York mixtures were applied as an overlay about 1.5 inches thick on top of the concrete roads.What the early results showedThe state didn't just pave the roads and walk away. The progress report covers the first three years of tests. Engineers recorded how the roads were behaving twice a year. They took note of the type and location of damage. They ran deflection tests, which measure how much a road flexes under heavy load. Lab tests provided additional data. The early results were not quite promising. The report states that the rubber pavements were not performing as well as the regular mixes. The federal guide agrees with the state's finding. After three years, the New York State Department of Transportation did not see either of the overlay projects as economical or successful.Other states had similar letdownsThe guide also provides information about the results from other states. Minnesota adopted the dry process on at least two projects since 1979. The roads performed well. However, they didn’t produce sufficient benefits to justify the higher cost. In Texas, one district’s rubber mix performed poorly and required a chip seal covering within three months. Washington State started using the dry process in 1977. The seven PlusRide road sections from Washington State varied from excellent to immediate failure. Eight dry process projects in Ontario, Canada generally performed poorly in the short term. The guide states that the results have been a mixed bag, with early failures being observed. It says that roads in service for several years showed little gain over regular overlays.What the story doesn't prove That is not to say that tyre rubber doesn’t belong on roads. Both New York projects tested only one technique, the dry process. Most of the crumb rubber data is from the wet process. That method mixes rubber into the asphalt itself. The dry-process projects above varied widely in performance across locations and climates, and the guide cites a lack of field data to evaluate the method’s performance. More carefully controlled test sections are needed in different climates to get further insight. The guide says such sections may need to be monitored for at least five years, and possibly as long as 30. Recycling a material isn’t the same as improving a road.
